verdict.rationale: Runpod's own docs show SSH access to Pods with full shell capabilities, which covers the core access part of the story. The pack never mentions bringing your own SSH keys or getting root-level control. Community comments that the execution environment is "locked down" are hedged ("might") and concern tunneling and remote-kernel setups, so they lower confidence but do not create a concrete dispute. Missing for 10: documentation of user-supplied SSH public keys, explicit root/privileged access to the environment, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can SSH into my GPU instance with my own keys and get root-level control of the environment

citations.quote: SSH provides secure, reliable access to your Pod for long-running processes and full shell capabilities.
Once deployed, you can connect to your Pod through SSH for command-line access
Access your Pod via SSH, JupyterLab, or VS Code.
